clue.text: Material for which the mason doesn't charge?

definitions.text: Material for which the mason doesn't charge?

parts.words: Material for which the mason doesn't charge?
parts.note: a fine-grained building stone that can be cut in any direction, read whimsically as stone the mason supplies at no cost

explanation.surface: A mason generously waives the bill for some building material.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine-grained sandstone or limestone that cuts easily in any direction is the mason's term for this material.

clue.text: Mrs Bridges' gem!

definitions.meaning: Mrs Bridges was the cook in the British TV drama Upstairs, Downstairs

explanation.surface: An exclamation about the cook's prized jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: Upstairs, Downstairs was a 1970s British TV series set in an Edwardian London house; Mrs Bridges was its cook and Ruby her kitchen maid.
explanation.definitionFit: The kitchen maid who worked for the cook in the TV series bore this name, and it is also a red precious stone.

clue.text: Drop in the ocean

parts.note: the idiom for a negligible amount, read literally as the falling of the sea level when the tide goes out

explanation.surface: The familiar phrase for something trifling.
explanation.definitionFit: The receding tide is a literal fall in sea level, a lowering of the water twice a day.

clue.text: Counted on everything being put into bonds

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, the word for everything going into the word for bonds

parts.note: to bond things is to tie them together, so bonded means tied
everything means all

explanation.surface: Someone relies on everything being invested in government bonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counted on' reads as relying on, but 'on' is only a link; the definition is 'Counted'.
explanation.definitionFit: To have reckoned up a total, as a scorer does, is this past tense verb.

clue.text: Should they be well chewed or bolted?

definitions.text: Should they be well chewed or bolted?

parts.words: Should they be well chewed or bolted?
parts.note: bolted suggests food gulped down, but it also means fastened by bolts, which these threaded fittings do alongside being edible kernels

explanation.surface: A question of table manners: should one chew food properly or gulp it?
explanation.definitionFit: Both edible kernels that are chewed and the threaded fasteners that go on bolts share this word.

clue.text: Concentration applied to France before Nazi invasion

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
the German Occupation of France began in 1940

explanation.surface: A historical note about the state of France just before the Germans arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'applied to France' sets the historical scene: France before the Occupation reads as the pre-Occupation period.
explanation.definitionFit: Absorption of the mind in a single matter is concentration on it.

clue.text: Architectural style for the righteous and upright

definitions.meaning: the late English Gothic style of church building, with strong vertical lines
standing at right angles to the horizontal, vertical

explanation.surface: A building style fitting for the morally upright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the righteous' plays on upright in its moral sense; the definition uses its sense of vertical.
explanation.definitionFit: Late English Gothic is named for its vertical tracery, and a vertical line is at right angles to the ground.

clue.text: Chances in favour of second rate skills

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
B is the grade for second rate, after A
skills are abilities

explanation.surface: Odds favouring mediocre skills.
explanation.definitionFit: Likelihoods of events happening are their chances.

clue.text: Canon one found in cannon

indicators.note: the numeral for one is located inside the word for artillery

parts.note: ordnance is artillery, big guns such as cannon
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A churchman found inside a gun, playing on canon and cannon.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a rule or decree, which is what an official order or by-law is.

clue.text: Take food in where date is seasoned

indicators.note: the word for taking food sits inside the word where

parts.note: taken as written
to take food is to eat

explanation.surface: An instruction to eat at the place where dates are spiced.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposed to the elements over time and toughened, like seasoned timber.

clue.text: Sharper cornered at the start of a chess game

definitions.meaning: a sharper is a cheat or swindler, as is a person who fleeces others

definitions.text: cornered at the start of a chess game
definitions.meaning: the castle piece in chess begins the game on a corner square

explanation.surface: A card cheat trapped as a chess game opens.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindler who cheats people out of money, and the chess piece also called the castle, which starts in a corner.

clue.text: Striking 6/6d

parts.note: six shillings and sixpence in old British money, written with Roman numerals for each six and d, the old penny abbreviation

explanation.surface: A price tag of six shillings and sixpence called striking.
explanation.walkthrough: Before 1971, British money was in shillings and pence, with d standing for pence; 6/6d is six and six, written VI VI D.
explanation.definitionFit: Vivid colours or images are bright and arresting, so they strike the eye.

clue.text: Earl gets 16th letter needed to…

parts.note: P is the sixteenth letter of the alphabet, spelt out as pee

explanation.surface: A nobleman given a letter is required to do something, continued in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on into 16 across: the sword is the thing 'needed to... fence'; the definition straddles both clues.
explanation.definitionFit: A fencing sword is what a fencer must have to take part in the sport.

clue.text: Vessels which Drake finished off before the Armada

definitions.text: which Drake finished off before the Armada
definitions.meaning: legend says Sir Francis Drake finished his game on Plymouth Hoe before sailing against the Spanish Armada

explanation.surface: Ships Drake destroyed before facing the Armada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' suggests ships in an Armada story; it means dishes. The lawn game with weighted balls is the one Drake supposedly completed.
explanation.definitionFit: Round dishes are vessels, and the lawn game played with weighted balls is the one Drake reportedly played.

clue.text: Liberal supports father of the Holy Father

indicators.note: in a down clue the letter for liberal sits beneath and holds up the word for father

parts.note: papa is a word for father

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician backs the father of the Pope.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the Pope, who is called the Holy Father, is the adjective meaning pontifical.

clue.text: … fence position where silly fieldsmen field

definitions.meaning: to put a fence round, an old spelling of enclose
in cricket, silly positions are fielding spots very near the batsman

explanation.surface: Fielders in cricket crowding near the bat, continuing the previous clue.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, 'silly' mid-on and the like are fielders placed very close to the batsman, so they field 'in close'.
explanation.definitionFit: To surround with a barrier is this old variant spelling, and read as two words it says near at hand, as close fielders stand.

clue.text: Granted disentanglement it could help police to search the lake

definitions.text: it could help police to search the lake

indicators.note: untangling the letters of granted lets them be laid out in a new order

explanation.surface: Granted, untangling something might help police searching a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A net dragged along the bottom of water to recover things is a tool police use in searches.

clue.text: A graduate heartened by pull of the flask

indicators.note: the heart of the graduate is filled with the word pull

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate
taken as written

explanation.surface: A graduate cheered by a swig from a flask.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-handled flask of Roman times, or a vessel for holy oil, is called an ampulla.

clue.text: Article quite frequently reproduced

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: reproduced means the letters of quite are made again in another order

explanation.surface: Something old and often copied.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: an old collector's piece is just the sort of article frequently reproduced as a copy.
explanation.definitionFit: Old collectable objects are commonly copied and sold as reproductions.

clue.text: Die broken after greenish blue poison

indicators.note: the broken letters of die come after the colour word

parts.note: cyan is a greenish-blue colour

indicators.note: broken means the letters of die are shattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A poisoner's grim colour-coded note about a broken die.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast-acting deadly compound, notorious in murder mysteries, is a poison.

clue.text: Boats which cleave the water

definitions.meaning: single-masted sailing vessels or small naval boats
things that cleave are things that cut, here slicing through the waves

explanation.surface: Ships slicing through the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Small fast sailing vessels bear this name, and anything that slices is one that cuts.

clue.text: Elder statesman who appealed to corporal punishment

parts.note: the cat, short for cat-o'-nine-tails, was a whip used for flogging
O is the interjection used in addressing or appealing to someone, as in O Lord

explanation.surface: A senior politician who called for flogging.
explanation.walkthrough: Cato the Elder was a stern Roman statesman; the joke is that he sounds like the cat-o'-nine-tails whip.
explanation.definitionFit: Cato the Elder, a Roman senator famed for austerity, is known by that epithet.

clue.text: Utter refutation of anarchy

definitions.meaning: to utter is to say or declare
anarchy is the absence of government, so organised government is its opposite

explanation.surface: A complete rebuttal of lawlessness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like an adjective meaning complete; it is the verb to say.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare is to say formally, and an organised political community with a government is the opposite of anarchy.

clue.text: Priest needed by the sick

definitions.meaning: the French word for a parish clergyman, a vicar or rector

explanation.surface: Ill people need a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A French parish priest is a curé, and a remedy restoring health is what the ill need.

clue.text: Be be singularly a goddess

parts.note: is is the singular third-person form of the verb to be
again the singular form, is

explanation.surface: A goddess spoken of in the singular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singularly' tells you to take each 'be' in its singular present form: he or she is.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian deity of motherhood and magic was a goddess.

clue.text: Roman emperor returning to the house

indicators.note: returning means the word to is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: A Roman emperor comes back to his house.
explanation.definitionFit: Otho ruled Rome briefly in AD 69, the Year of the Four Emperors.

clue.text: Following with clean question otherwise put

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are put in another order, arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A clean question phrased differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that results from or follows on from something else is a consequence of it.

clue.text: Malicious remark in the way that person takes one in

parts.note: as means in the way that

indicators.note: takes one in means the word person holds the numeral inside it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A nasty comment about how someone takes people in.
explanation.definitionFit: A slur or damaging insinuation against someone's character is a malicious remark.
